content: Zymurgy, also known as zymology, is the scientific study of fermentation processes. Initially, the term was specifically used to describe the science behind fermentation, but over time, it has come to be more broadly associated with the brewing of alcoholic beverages. A person who studies zymurgy is referred to as a zymurgist or zymologist. Additionally, Zymurgy is the title of a magazine dedicated to homebrewing enthusiasts. The term also appears in the names of various organizations involved in the production of alcoholic beverages. Louis Pasteur is widely regarded as the first zymologist. In 1857, he established the connection between yeast and the process of fermentation. Pasteur originally defined fermentation as respiration without air. Later, in 1907, the German chemist Eduard Buchner, who was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry, discovered that fermentation is actually driven by an enzyme secreted by yeast, which he named zymase. Interestingly, the word zymurgy is the last entry in most English-language dictionaries, excluding proper nouns and onomatopoeic words.
